title: Adversarial by Origin How the Classification of External Influence on Machine Meaning Becomes Law Without Becoming Jurisprudence
creator: Johannes Sigil; contributing editor Lee Sharks
description:
A provisional v1.0 legal-theoretical paper by Johannes Sigil, edited by Lee Sharks, arguing that emerging AI-security taxonomies increasingly classify influence on machine meaning by **origin rather than harm**. Under the paper’s model, platform-originated shaping is called alignment, curation, or safety, while externally originated shaping is called injection, poisoning, or manipulation—even where no unauthorized access, fraud, destructive command, or concrete injury is present.

The paper traces possible formalization through statutes, standards, procurement, executive instruments, platform terms, pleadings, settlements, and enforcement practice rather than through a fully charged, defended, appealed, and digested jurisprudential cycle. It proposes harm-based classification, contemporaneous adversarial records, test cases, foreign proxy cycles, and intervention at the standards layer. These are the paper’s legal and political arguments, not legal advice or a verified prediction that courts will adopt the proposed origin-based theory.
